actions.reason: Strong biological support: RNA shows FDR-significant upregulation of interferon/inflammatory pathways with large effect sizes, and WXS shows significant BAP1 enrichment (q=0.0044). These two distinct modalities provide meaningful corroboration of the set's identity. Confounder analysis shows a strong site-specific association (CJ), but this is a single technical factor and does not negate the coherent biological signal. Structural metrics show moderate support (median support count=3, resampling ARI=0.636). No better-supported structural action or resolvable evidence gap exists.

Biological support is absent across all modalities (no significant RNA, WXS, or CNV findings). The set is strongly confounded by technical factors (SIEMENS manufacturer, scanner model, kernel) with FDR-significant associations, indicating the set is likely defined by technical variation rather than biology. Cross-modal consistency shows the set is driven almost entirely by CT (median silhouette=0.276) with no support from other modalities. No supported split or merge exists, and no available extra evidence can resolve the technical confounding. Drop is the appropriate action.

Biological support is absent across all modalities (no significant RNA, WXS, or CNV findings). Cross-modal consistency shows weak cohesion with near-zero silhouettes in most modalities and only slight WSI support. No technical confounders are significant, but the lack of any biological distinction and weak structural support indicate the set does not have a defensible identity. No supported split or merge exists, and no available extra evidence can resolve the gap. Drop is the appropriate action.

Biological support is coherent across RNA and CNV: RNA shows extensive FDR-significant pathway enrichment (25/50 pathways) with large effect sizes, and CNV shows consistent lower copy-number on multiple chromosomal arms with FDR significance. These two distinct modalities provide meaningful corroboration. Confounder analysis shows no significant per-set technical associations (q=0.065 trends are not significant). Structural metrics show moderate support (resampling ARI=0.561, consensus separation=0.624). No better-supported structural action or resolvable evidence gap exists.

Biological support is primarily transcriptional with strong RNA pathway enrichment (18/50 pathways, large effect sizes), but WXS and CNV show only nominal trends. However, the RNA findings are coherent and FDR-significant, and confounder analysis shows no significant technical associations. Cross-modal consistency shows RNA provides the strongest separation (pair median silhouette=0.045 vs C0002). While genomic support is weak, the RNA evidence is strong and not contradicted by other modalities. No supported split or merge exists, and no available extra evidence can resolve the gap. Accept is justified given the strong RNA signal and absence of technical confounding.
